column1: # VS Code extensions that shipped malware. One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   id        publisher.name, as the extension's folder spells it (compared without case)
#   version   the exact version, or * when every version is malware
#   incident  an id from data/incidents.tsv, whose level must be act
#   registry  openvsx: the bad build was only ever published to Open VSX, so it is looked for in the
#             extension folders of the editors that install from there (Cursor, Windsurf and Devin
#             Desktop, VSCodium, Kiro and Antigravity) and not in VS Code's own, where the same id is the
#             Marketplace's extension, or another publisher's. any: looked for in every folder. An id
#             that Microsoft's list of extensions removed from the Marketplace names
#             (github.com/microsoft/vsmarketplace, RemovedPackages.md) was on the Marketplace too, so it
#             is any. Of the openvsx ids, the Marketplace offers only the oorzc extensions (October 2026).
#   os        all, mac, linux or win, or two of them separated by a comma (mac,win): where the
#             extension's malware could run, as its source says. It is looked for on every OS; on one
#             where its malware could not run, the report shows it as a malicious extension to remove,
#             not a compromised machine (as data/bad-pypi.tsv's os does)
# Looked for as <id>-<version> folders (a platform suffix such as -darwin-arm64 may follow).
# GlassWorm, from Socket's posts and one of Aikido's, each its own incident. A version where the post gives one, every
# version (*) where it names the extension without one: these are the attacker's own extensions, which
# update themselves, so a version from before an extension was turned counts too. Left out: what a post
# calls a sleeper (not malicious yet), the 17 extensions turned on 29 April, whose payload Open VSX
# had already removed (the April post's update), and three themes of the October cluster that
# Microsoft's list removes as malware (1 and 2 October 2026): charcoal-mint-studio.theme-charcoal-mint,
# lohsebhipolg2s.theme-aurora-borealis and holiday-themes.theme-coca-cola-christmas. Socket found no
# payload in the versions it read and calls Coca-Cola Christmas malware for its cluster, not a payload;
# a removal from the Marketplace does not say what ran on a machine, nor anything of the Open VSX
# builds; and Charcoal Mint's three builds on Open VSX hold colors and, in 1.0.2, a welcome page.
#   January 2026: the four oorzc extensions, Open VSX only: Socket's findings concern the Open VSX
#     builds, and it does not suggest the publisher's Marketplace listings were compromised. The
#     Marketplace still offers them, oorzc.ssh-tools with a 0.5.1 of 30 March 2026, after that post:
#     Microsoft's list of removed extensions does not name it (24 October 2026), and its package
#     holds none of the loader IOCs Socket publishes (the AES key and IVs, the Solana address, the
#     IP). Three at their malicious versions, and oorzc.ssh-tools at every version: Open VSX removed them all and added it
#     to its malware list, Socket says. Their os is mac: Socket shows their loader going on only when
#     os.platform() is darwin, to a second stage that is a macOS implant. And the thirteen earlier
#     extensions it lists, which the Marketplace does not offer and Microsoft's list does not name
#     (all: the post does not show what their code checks).
#   13 March 2026: the 72 extensions listed since that report, less those thirteen. Four were on the
#     Marketplace too: Microsoft's list removes Lavender-Studio.theme-lavender-dreams as malware (2
#     October 2026), and the dopbop-studio, kwitch-studio and potstok ones as impersonation (3 March
#     2026). Whether those Marketplace builds carried the loader is not known: they are any.
#   18 March 2026: the versions the post shows delivering malware, themselves or through an extension pack.
#     Not the rest of its weekend wave of 14 and 15 March: the post lists 17 impersonation extensions
#     without showing those versions deliver malware, and Socket's campaign page lists them among its
#     affected artifacts with no word on which are malware and which sleepers. Three of them, later made
#     into extension packs that delivered it, are listed at those versions, and one more from Aikido's
#     post, which shows it delivering malware (below).
#   25 April 2026: the six it confirms as malicious; its 67 sleepers are left out. The post shows
#     boulderzitunnel.vscode-buddies loading its native installer only on win32 and darwin, so its
#   Aikido, April 2026 (glasswormzig, its post of 8 April, updated 21 April):
#     specstudio.code-wakatime-activity-tracker, an Open VSX extension of that weekend wave, loads a native
#     binary that installs floktokbok.autoimport, a GlassWorm dropper, from GitHub into every editor it
#     finds, VS Code included, so that one is any. The tracker loads win.node on Windows and mac.node
#     anywhere else, so its malware runs on Windows and macOS only: mac,win. Aikido says to treat a
#     machine with either as compromised, and gives no version: every version.
#   2 October 2026: the two malicious Marketplace themes (Cosmic Nebula is on Open VSX too; the other,
#     microsoftvs.microsoftvs, hid a Windows downloader that ran a batch file through cmd.exe).
